Description: Single price for all features — no tiers or complexity

Keywords: grand slam offer,hormozi,value equation,dream outcome,perceived likelihood,time delay,effort sacrifice,offer design
Description: Value = (Dream Outcome × Perceived Likelihood) ÷ (Time Delay × Effort). Maximize numerator by selling the outcome not the tool. Minimize denominator by removing friction and delivering fast results.
Best_For: Designing irresistible offers that make price irrelevant — works for every pricing model
Pros: Makes price irrelevant (value-based)|Eliminates objections systematically|Creates word-of-mouth through outcome delivery
Cons: Requires deep customer understanding|Over-promising risks trust|Done-for-you models have margin pressure
Example_Companies: Hormozi portfolio companies|HubSpot (outcome-focused pricing)|Superhuman (/mo but 10x speed promise)
Giantiny_Note: Giantiny ④ — outcome-based pricing naturally generates profit because value perceived >> cost

Keywords: problem list,solution list,delivery vehicle,offer packaging,done for you,done with you,self serve,offer stack
Description: Step 1: List ALL customer problems (from Monkey Problem + Weakchain). Step 2: Create specific solution for each. Step 3: Choose delivery vehicle (self-serve vs done-with-you vs done-for-you). Step 4: Package with outcome-focused name + value-based price + risk-reversing guarantee.
Best_For: Converting a validated idea into a sellable offer — the bridge between validation and revenue
Pros: Systematic (not creative guessing)|Directly uses validation data|Creates offer that sells itself
Cons: Takes time to map all problems|May overwhelm solo founder|Guarantee design requires confidence in delivery
Example_Companies: Remote Momentum System (7-day setup guarantee)|Alex Hormozi Gym Launch (fill your gym in 30 days)
Giantiny_Note: Use structural gaps from competitor analysis to choose delivery vehicle they CANNOT copy

Keywords: guarantee,risk reversal,money back,outcome guarantee,conditional guarantee,unconditional,trust building,do nothing cost
Description: Use Do-nothing Scenario data to design guarantees. If inaction costs $X/month the guarantee should promise to prevent that loss. Types: Unconditional (30-day refund) Conditional (result or money back) Performance (hit metric X or free). The stronger the Do-nothing cost the bolder the guarantee can be.
Best_For: Removing last objection to purchase — especially effective when Do-nothing cost is quantifiable
Pros: Eliminates purchase risk|Forces you to deliver real results|Creates trust before relationship
Cons: Bad product + strong guarantee = financial disaster|Must have ops to fulfill|Conditional guarantees need clear metrics
Example_Companies: Dominos (30 min or free)|Basecamp (30-day refund no questions)|Hormozi (result-based guarantees)
Giantiny_Note: Giantiny ④ — guarantee backed by real delivery creates compound trust (organic growth)
